title: IEC 60335-2-8 Electric Shaver Testing India
description: IEC 60335-2-8:2022 electric shaver safety testing in India for electric shock, heating, moisture, abnormaloperation and mechanical safety with ITC India.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: ITC India provides IEC 60335-2-8 testing for electric shavers, hair clippers and similar personal-care appliances intended for household and similar use. The current IEC 60335-2-8:2022 standard defines particular safety requirements for these appliances and is applied together with the relevant general requirements of IEC 60335-1.

Electric grooming appliances may combine motors, rechargeable batteries, external power supplies, cutting mechanisms, electrical insulation and components that can be exposed to moisture. Safety testing helps manufacturers identify electrical, thermal, mechanical and fire-related hazards before certification, market entry or large-scale production.
ITC India also provides broader household equipment testing for electrical appliances covered by the IEC 60335 series.

sections.heading: What Is IEC 60335-2-8?
paragraphs: IEC 60335-2-8 is the product-specific safety standard for electric shavers, hair clippers, epilators, manicure and pedicure appliances and similar products.

The standard covers applicable mains-powered, DC-supplied and battery-operated appliances with rated voltages up to 250 V. Certain similar appliances used by laypersons outside the normal home environment may also fall within its scope.

IEC 60335-2-8 should be used together with the applicable requirements of IEC 60335-1. Manufacturers planning complete compliance testing can therefore also review ITC India’s IEC 60335-1 safety testing services.

sections.heading: Protection Against Electric Shock
paragraphs: Personal-care appliances are frequently handled close to the body, so protection against access to hazardous live parts is an important safety consideration.
Testing can evaluate enclosure construction, insulation systems, accessible conductive parts, protective separation and other measures intended to reduce electric-shock risk.
For rechargeable models, the safety assessment should also consider charging arrangements, detachable power-supply parts, connectors and low-voltage circuits where applicable.
ITC India provides broader electrical testing services for electrical and electronic products requiring safety evaluation.

sections.heading: Heating and Temperature-Rise Testing
paragraphs: Electric shavers and clippers contain motors, batteries, electronic circuits and moving cutting parts that can generate heat during operation.

Heating tests evaluate temperatures at relevant parts while the appliance operates under specified conditions. Excessive temperature can damage insulation, affect battery life, deform plastics or create an uncomfortable or unsafe accessible surface.
For animal shearers or similar high-duty products, blade and enclosure temperatures can also be important depending on the appliance construction and applicable requirements.

sections.heading: Leakage Current and Electric Strength
paragraphs: The insulation system of a mains-powered or rechargeable grooming appliance must provide adequate protection throughout normal use.

Leakage-current measurements help determine whether accessible current remains within specified limits. Electric-strength testing evaluates whether electrical insulation can withstand the required test voltage without breakdown.
These checks can be performed at the stages defined by IEC 60335-1 and the applicable Part 2 requirements.

sections.heading: Moisture Resistance and Wet-Use Appliances
paragraphs: Some electric shavers and personal-care appliances are designed for use in bathrooms, near water or under wet-use conditions.

Where applicable to the product design and intended use, moisture-resistance testing helps evaluate whether foreseeable exposure to water or humidity compromises insulation or creates an electric-shock hazard.
Seals, enclosure joints, charging arrangements and user instructions should be consistent with the intended operating environment.
Products should only carry wet-use or washable claims when the construction and applicable compliance requirements support those claims.

sections.heading: Abnormal Operation Testing
paragraphs: Safe operation must also be considered when foreseeable faults or abnormal conditions occur.

Depending on the appliance, abnormal-operation evaluation can address conditions such as motor restriction, stalled moving parts, charging faults or failure of temperature-control or protective components.
The objective is to ensure that a foreseeable abnormal condition does not result in excessive temperature, fire, electric shock or another unacceptable hazard.

sections.heading: Mechanical Safety of Shavers and Hair Clippers
paragraphs: Shavers and clippers incorporate high-speed motors and moving blades, making mechanical safety an important part of product evaluation.
Testing and inspection can consider accessible moving parts, blade assemblies, guards, attachments, switches and the mechanical strength of the enclosure.
Components should remain securely mounted during foreseeable use, and damage to the appliance should not expose hazardous electrical or mechanical parts.

sections.heading: Construction, Wiring and Components
paragraphs: Compliance depends on the safety of the complete appliance, not just its motor or cutting system.
Evaluation can include internal wiring, electrical connections, supply or charging cords, switches, batteries, connectors, insulation, screws, terminals, creepage distances and clearances.
The 2022 edition also includes updated requirements relating to detachable power-supply parts and certain Class III appliance constructions.
Materials near electrical components should also provide suitable resistance to heat and fire under applicable test conditions.

sections.heading: Battery-Operated and Rechargeable Shavers
paragraphs: Many modern shavers and grooming appliances use rechargeable batteries and external chargers.
Manufacturers should provide information about the battery system, charging circuit, adapter or detachable power supply and protective electronics when submitting the appliance for testing.
Where separate battery standards or transport requirements apply to lithium-ion batteries, those requirements should be evaluated independently from IEC 60335-2-8 appliance safety testing.

sections.heading: EMC Testing for Electronic Personal-Care Appliances
paragraphs: Modern grooming products may contain electronic speed controls, battery-management circuits, displays, switching power supplies or wireless functions.

Electromagnetic compatibility may therefore be required separately for the intended market. ITC India provides EMC/EMI testing services for consumer electrical and electronic products requiring emissions and immunity evaluation.

sections.heading: Products Covered
paragraphs: IEC 60335-2-8 can apply to electric shavers, hair clippers, epilators, manicure appliances, pedicure appliances, animal clippers, animal shearers and similar electrical grooming products where they fall within the standard’s scope.
The applicable standard should always be confirmed against the product’s intended use and construction before testing begins.

sections.heading: Information Required for Testing
paragraphs: Manufacturers should provide the model number, rated voltage and power, supply type, appliance class, battery information, charger specifications, motor details, circuit diagrams, critical component list, construction drawings and user instructions.
For washable or wet-use products, details of the intended water-exposure conditions and product markings should also be supplied.

sections.heading: Why Choose ITC India?
paragraphs: ITC India supports manufacturers with household-appliance and electrical-safety testing covering electrical, thermal, mechanical and construction-related requirements.
Reviewing technical documentation before testing helps establish the correct standard edition, sample configuration and required safety evaluations.

sections.heading: Request IEC 60335-2-8 Testing
paragraphs: For IEC 60335-2-8:2022 electric shaver and hair clipper safety testing, send your testing requirement to ITC India with the product specifications, electrical ratings, battery or charger information and required compliance standard.

sections.heading: What is IEC 60335-2-8?
paragraphs: IEC 60335-2-8 is the international safety standard containing particular requirements for electric shavers, hair clippers and similar personal-care appliances.

sections.heading: What is the latest edition of IEC 60335-2-8?
paragraphs: The current edition is IEC 60335-2-8:2022, Edition 7.0.

sections.heading: Which products are covered by IEC 60335-2-8?
paragraphs: The scope includes electric shavers, hair clippers, epilators, manicure and pedicure appliances and certain similar grooming appliances.

sections.heading: Does IEC 60335-2-8 cover rechargeable shavers?
paragraphs: Yes. The current standard can cover applicable battery-operated and DC-supplied appliances, including products using detachable power-supply parts.

sections.heading: What safety tests are important for electric shavers?
paragraphs: Typical evaluation areas include protection against electric shock, heating, leakage current, electric strength, moisture resistance, abnormal operation, mechanical safety, construction, wiring and resistance to heat and fire.
